section_entries.label: 3. Bicomplex Riemann zeta function
section_entries.mathematical_role: Defines bicomplex powers and the Dirichlet series, proves componentwise convergence, constructs the maximal holomorphic continuation, proves uniqueness, and locates its polar divisor.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Bicomplex exponentiation reduced to idempotent complex powers
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Defining n^w through the bicomplex exponential makes the Dirichlet series meaningful and immediately exposes its two ordinary complex-power components. This is the construction that connects algebraic representation to analytic convergence.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Componentwise continuation on the complement of the translated zero-divisor set
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The continued bicomplex zeta is assembled from two classical continuations. Identifying the domain as a product of punctured complex planes proves openness and connectedness, componentwise holomorphic reconstruction proves T-holomorphicity, and the several-variable identity theorem yields uniqueness.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Once bicomplex objects split into two orthogonal complex components, convergence, holomorphic continuation, zeros, and Euler factorization are transported by applying the classical construction separately and recombining.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: This is a within-source structural synthesis, not evidence that every complex-analytic property transfers; zero divisors and domain topology create explicit failures.
